blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ ﵁ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ إِذَا قَامَ يُصَلِّي أَقْبَلَ اللهُ عَلَيْهِ بِوَجْهِهِ حَتَّي يَنْقَلِبَ أَوْ يُحْدِثَ حَدَثَ سُوءٍ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه ابن ماجه باب المصلي يتنخم رقم:١٠٢٣
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Hudhaifah (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said, “When a person stands to pray, Allah too turns His full attention towards him until he finishes his Salah or until he engages in something that disturbs the devotion (in the Salah).”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ ﵁ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: إِذَا قَامَ أَحَدُكُمْ إِلَي الصَّلوةِ فَلَا يَمْسَحِ الْحَصَي فَإِنَّ الرَّحْمَةَ تُوَاجِهُهُ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه الترمذي وقال:حديث ابي ذر حديث حسن باب ماجاء في كراهية مسح الحصي ....رقم:٣٧٩
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said, “When one of you stands to pray, he should not needlessly move the pebbles during the Salah. For, at the time of Salah, the special mercy (Rahmah) of Allah turns towards him.”

blocks.text: Explanation: In the early period of Islam, pebbles were spread in the masjids, and at times, when the stones were standing upright, it was difficult to make sajdah. That time (of praying) is the time when the mercy of Allah turns towards one. Since moving the stones or engaging in other such actions at that time would cause one to miss the mercy of Allah, the Prophet ﷺ forbade moving the stones repeatedly.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ سَمُرَةَ ﵁ قَالَ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ يَاْمُرُنَا إِذَا كُنَّا فِي الصَّلوةِ وَرَفَعْنَا رُؤُوسَنَا مِنَ السُّجُودِ أَنْ نَطْمَئِنَّ عَلَي اْلاَرْضِ جُلُوساً
